subject: Social Media
title: Election Interference Worldwide
description: A quick win: understand Election Interference Worldwide.

hook.text: In 2016, fake news flooded America's election. By 2020, 80 countries had documented online election interference.

buildup.text: Oxford researchers found organized social media manipulation in every continent. It's a global phenomenon.

discovery.text: Tools are cheap. A botnet costs $500. Fake news sites cost nothing. Even small countries can run campaigns.

twist.text: The biggest campaigns aren't foreign. Governments manipulate their own citizens' feeds to stay in power.

climax.text: Philippines, Brazil, India, Turkey—each election now features paid troll armies. Democracy and social media clash.

punchline.text: Election interference isn't a bug. It's a feature of the platform.

quiz.question: Who runs the biggest social media manipulation campaigns?
